## Process Overview

The Outcomes Framework process is split into two stages:

### User / Data Owner Responsibilities
- Identify the indicator source  
- Complete metadata  
- Confirm lookup requirements  
- Prepare or submit the dataset  

### Analyst / Data Team Responsibilities
- Load metadata into the database  
- Update reference tables where required  
- Generate reference population data  
- Update age metadata  
- Load data into staging tables  
- Run the R calculation process  
- Validate calculated values  
- Publish outputs to the final processed table  


## User / Data Owner Responsibilities

### Identify the Data Source

Determine the source of the indicator to identify the appropriate landing route:

- **SQL**: Data from the data warehouse  
- **API**: Data pulled via API (e.g. Fingertips)  
- **SharePoint**: Data from external providers or pre-calculated data using the standard template  
- **Other**: Any other source  


### Complete Indicator Metadata

Update the metadata control file with all required information for the new indicator.

- The `indicator_id` must be the next sequential ID (increment from the most recent ID)  
- Ensure all key fields are completed, especially:

  - `indicator_id`  
  - `age`  
  - `population_type`  
  - `sex`  
  - `imd`  
  - `geography` 
  - `precalculated`  


### Confirm Lookup Requirements

Check whether required lookup values already exist, including:

- Age bands  
- Geography codes  
- Sex codes  
- IMD codes  
- Population type  

If new lookup values are required, request that they are added before the data is processed.


### Prepare or Submit the Dataset

Prepare the dataset in the required standard format.

Refer to the official [guidelines](https://birmingham-and-solihull-ics.github.io/2_BSOL_Outcomes_Framework/R/OF_process_documentation.html#ch1-sec-update-final-table).

If the data is pre-calculated or provided externally, submit it using the latest standard data entry template:  [Data Entry Template](https://birminghamandsolihullccg.sharepoint.com/:x:/r/sites/BirminghamandSolihullIntegratedIntelligenceHub/Shared%20Documents/Outcomes%20Framework%20Rebuild/Data/Data%20Entry%20Template/data_entry_template.xlsx?d=wddf3ec3cb71d4303a60e4899dca4986b&csf=1&web=1&e=kaPIZX).

Before loading data into the landing table, confirm that:

- indicator IDs are correct  
- reused SQL scripts have been updated to avoid mismatches  
- column names and data types match the expected structure  


## Analyst / Data Team Responsibilities

### Review Submitted Metadata and Dataset

Review the submitted metadata and dataset to ensure:

- required fields are complete  
- indicator IDs are correct  
- age bands match the reference table  
- dataset structure follows the standard format  
- values are suitable for processing  

Load the updated metadata into the database.


### Update Lookup and Reference Tables

Where new lookup values are required, update the relevant lookup file and load the updated reference data into the database.

This includes:

- age group reference table  
- geography reference table  
- value type reference table  
- other relevant lookup tables  


### Generate Denominators and Update Age Metadata

Once the new data has been added to the landing table:

- Generate Census-based denominators where required  
- Update the age metadata  

This includes:

- updating population denominators, particularly when new age bands are introduced  
- generating age metadata for DASR indicators  


### Load Data into the Staging Table and Run Calculation Process

Insert the new indicator data into the appropriate staging table and run the R calculation process.

This includes:

- combining data from multiple landing tables into a unified staging table  
- running the R process to calculate:
  - crude rates  
  - directly age-standardised rates (DASR)  
  - counts  
  - percentages  
  - other required metrics  
- confirming that calculations have completed successfully  



### Validate and Publish Outputs

Review the calculated outputs before publishing.

Validation checks should include:

- no missing values where values are expected  
- correct denominators used  
- correct age, sex, geography, IMD, and population filters applied  
- values are reasonable compared to previous periods  
- caveats and notes are documented  

Once validation is complete, publish the output to the final processed table.



## Simplified Flowchart

```{mermaid}
%%| fig-width: 6
%%| fig-align: center
%%| 
flowchart TD

    A(Start) --> B[User: Identify Indicator Source]
    B --> C[User: Complete Metadata]
    C --> D[User: Confirm Lookup Requirements]
    D --> E[User: Prepare or Submit Dataset]

    E --> F[Analyst: Review Metadata and Dataset]
    F --> G[Analyst: Update Lookups and Reference Tables]
    G --> H[Analyst: Load Data to Landing Table]
    H --> I[Analyst: Generate Denominators & Age Metadata]
    I --> J[Analyst: Load to Staging Table]
    J --> K[Analyst: Run R Calculation Process]
    K --> L[Analyst: Validate Outputs]
    L --> M[Analyst: Publish to Final Table]
    M --> N(End)

    %% Styles

    %% Start (Green)
    classDef startNode fill:#4CAF50,stroke:#2E7D32,color:#ffffff,stroke-width:2px;

    %% End (Orange)
    classDef endNode fill:#FFB74D,stroke:#EF6C00,color:#000000,stroke-width:2px;

    %% User (Blue)
    classDef user fill:#E3F2FD,stroke:#1E88E5,color:#000,stroke-width:1.5px;

    %% Analyst (Pink)
    classDef analyst fill:#FCE4EC,stroke:#D81B60,color:#000,stroke-width:1.5px;

    %% Apply Styles

    class A startNode;
    class N endNode;

    class B,C,D,E user;
    class F,G,H,I,J,K,L,M analyst;
```
